title: Website and Zone Builder reliability fixes
content:
Zone Builder

  • Proc requests stay within their zone. Editing or deleting a request through another zone is rejected. Failed deletions retain the request and its mentions together, and a request deleted during an edit no longer sends an assignment or status notification.
  • Keep discussions together. Comments stay within their zone and discussion. Deleting a discussion either removes the full discussion and its mentions or keeps them all when the operation fails. New replies cannot attach to a parent that is being deleted.
  • Edit requests and comments again. Saving proc-request edits, changing status and editing comments now use the correct website requests. Builder API filters use the expected field names, and read-notification filters return the matching messages and totals.
  • Keep proc-request discussion history. Deleting a request keeps its comments and replies as general zone discussion, including their existing mentions. A failed deletion retains the original request and discussion together.

Website Changelog

  • Publish once and keep drafts private. Concurrent saves no longer trigger duplicate publication announcements or accidentally publish a competing draft. Announcements use the release title saved when publishing, so later unpublished draft titles stay private.

Dashboard and administration

  • Consistent request handling. Admin connection, permission and analytics pages use the shared website request handling. Dashboard boot-time reads also use the configured API address and login cookies, with a timeout and the usual unavailable notice when needed.

Administration

  • Safer image publication. Site logos, hero images and profile image replacements preserve the published object until the replacement URL is saved. Concurrent uploads use unique objects, and cleanup targets only the previous published image.
  • Clear failures. Invalid numeric settings are rejected before persistence; failed log downloads end safely and admin failures retain useful messages without exposing internal diagnostics.

Builder and operator tools

  • Scoped zone commits. A zone commit includes only that zone’s files and preserves unrelated staged work. Status reads stay scoped, tracked deletions are included, and refs and messages are treated literally.
  • Contained stream failures. Failed zone downloads and launcher errors are handled safely. Unexpected operator failures show a support reference and keep uncertain process state explicit.

Live server logs

  • Reliable live subscriptions. Log tails use the WebSocket capability, confirm Live only after the server accepts the subscription, and retire old selections or connections.
  • Safe bounded reads. Short reads cannot expose unwritten bytes, failures end the live indication, and appends are processed in bounded chunks while keeping Unicode characters intact. The viewer retains recent lines with complete history available through the existing download.

Connection privacy

  • Keep addresses scoped. Real-time connection events omit player IP addresses. Detailed connection history remains behind its existing permission checks, and failure diagnostics exclude driver SQL and bindings.

Session and permission changes

  • End access when a session ends. Logout and password changes end matching application sockets. Permission changes refresh open sockets, remove denied log watchers and end terminals that lost access.
  • Respect newer logins. Background checks cannot replace or close a newer authenticated identity, and stalled checks end safely without adding repeated database work.
